claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys is governed by VEC-mediated modulation of chemical short-range order.
Higher VEC stabilizes the disordered FCC phase.
Increasing Al content lowers VEC.
Lower VEC caused by increasing Al promotes ordered intermetallic-phase formation.
Ordered intermetallic phases undermine the alloy's advantageous properties.
The proposed near-equiatomic initial alloy is single-phase FCC after high-temperature homogenization.
Chemical short-range order influences the formation or suppression of B2 or sigma phases within the FCC matrix.
The reduction in VEC caused by additional Al modifies the electronic bonding environment.
The modified electronic bonding environment increases the driving force for atomic ordering.
Enhanced atomic ordering promotes ordered intermetallic-phase formation.
Formation of ordered intermetallic phases destabilizes the FCC structure.
Ordered intermetallic-phase formation degrades mechanical and environmental properties.
Lower Al and the resulting higher VEC disrupt atomic ordering.
Suppression of ordering by lower Al stabilizes the FCC phase.
High-Al samples will exhibit an earlier onset of ordered intermetallic-phase formation during isothermal holding than low-Al samples.
High-Al samples will develop a higher fraction of ordered intermetallic phases than low-Al samples.
High-Al samples will have lower high-temperature strength, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness than low-Al samples.
The near-equiatomic, intermediate-Al baseline remains single-phase FCC under the specified homogenization, cooling, and isothermal-hold conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies over approximately 10–30 at.% Al, where VEC changes are sufficient to affect short-range order without compositional imbalance independently causing phase separation.
The VEC threshold for ordering may vary because of interactions among the constituent elements and minor alloying effects.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome calls the low-Al alloy the baseline, whereas the baseline field defines an intermediate-Al near-equiatomic alloy as the baseline.
The intervention specifies two alloy variants, but the falsification design specifies two systematically varied series, leaving the number and structure of comparison groups inconsistent.
